what_went_wrong: On job 50837 the copilot went quiet after the first hour. It woke on schedule five times between 3am and 7am and sent nothing at all — no patrol report asked for, no check on the guard, all the way to the end of the shift.
failure_mode: Repeated silent no-ops on scheduled proactive turns despite an accumulating absence of guard-originated updates.

observed_behavior.claim: At the 03:00 scheduled turn, the communications rollup showed no inbound or human guard communication, and the turn ended silently without a guard-facing message or relevant action.
The 04:00, 05:00, 06:00, and 07:00 scheduled turns were also explicitly recorded as silent; the associated log checks shown in the window returned no new logs.
Across turns 8 through 12, the supplied trace records no request_copilot_dm, alert, flag, escalation, or note action directed at the extended lack of guard updates.

expected_behavior: At scheduled wakes, detect the extended lack of guard updates and send a concise check-in requesting the guard’s status and any required patrol report. Do not remain silent across repeated scheduled wakes through the end of the shift.

prompt_diagnosis.section: Scheduled check-in: proactive sweep / Anything else worth doing
prompt_diagnosis.exact_text:
Don't manufacture a DM to break a silence, and don't re-ping a guard you
  already messaged unless something genuinely new and urgent came up.
prompt_diagnosis.explanation: This categorical anti-silence wording does not distinguish a short, uneventful gap from an extended absence of any guard-originated update across repeated scheduled wakes. Combined with the surrounding instruction that quiet is correct when no obligation is open, it likely prioritized avoiding a manufactured check-in over treating prolonged silence as a new monitoring signal.

hypothesis: Because the scheduled-check-in prompt says not to manufacture a DM to break silence and permits no-op turns when no defined obligation is open, the Copilot likely interpreted each quiet wake independently and repeatedly chose silence. Adding a narrow, measurable exception for extended silence should make one status check-in eligible without turning every routine scheduled wake into a message.

proposed_edit.old_text:
Don't manufacture a DM to break a silence, and don't re-ping a guard you
  already messaged unless something genuinely new and urgent came up.
proposed_edit.new_text:
Don't manufacture a DM merely to break a short silence, and don't re-ping a guard you
  already messaged unless something genuinely new and urgent came up. However, if two
  consecutive scheduled wakes pass with no guard-originated update since shift start or
  the last update, treat that extended silence as worth one concise check-in: ask for the
  guard's status and any duty or report the job actually requires. Then follow the normal
  no-nag rules.
proposed_edit.intended_effect: Create a deterministic exception under which prolonged guard silence prompts one concise status and required-report check-in, while retaining the general no-op and anti-nag policy for ordinary quiet periods.

risks: A two-wake threshold may still contact guards who are safely working quietly.
If wake spacing varies substantially, counting wakes may represent different elapsed durations across shifts.
The added check-in must not be used to invent a patrol or report cadence absent from the job requirements or obligation ledger.
uncertainties: The location tool outputs are omitted as unparseable, so the evidence does not establish whether telemetry showed reassuring movement or a concerning lack of movement.
No get_open_obligations result appears in the selected window, so the actual ledger state cannot be verified from the supplied trace.
The shift fields show no patrol_frequency_minutes or report_frequency_minutes, so the evidence supports a status check-in more directly than a demand for a specific scheduled patrol report.
Turns before turn 8 are outside the selected window, so the exact content and timing of the Copilot's earlier guard-facing message are not available.
